classification.difficultyReason: Rearrange linear trigonometric equations, calculate related angles and select both solutions using quadrant signs.

content.prompt: Solve each equation for $0^\circ\le\theta\le360^\circ$, correct to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
The related angle is $\alpha=\sin^{-1}(0.58778)\approx35.9996^\circ$. Sine is positive in quadrants I and II.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=\alpha\approx36^\circ\\\theta&=180^\circ-\alpha\approx144^\circ\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{1.6776}{3}\\\cos\theta&=0.5592\end{align*}$$

The related angle is $\alpha=\cos^{-1}(0.5592)\approx55.9995^\circ$. Cosine is positive in quadrants I and IV.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=\alpha\approx56^\circ\\\theta&=360^\circ-\alpha\approx304^\circ\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\sin\theta&=\frac{4.455}{5}\\\sin\theta&=0.891\end{align*}$$

The related angle is $\alpha=\sin^{-1}(0.891)\approx62.9992^\circ$. Sine is positive in quadrants I and II.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=\alpha\approx63^\circ\\\theta&=180^\circ-\alpha\approx117^\circ\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\sin\theta&=\frac{-1.4863}{2}\\\sin\theta&=-0.74315\end{align*}$$

The related angle is $\alpha=\sin^{-1}(0.74315)\approx48.0004^\circ$. Sine is negative in quadrants III and IV.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ+\alpha\approx228^\circ\\\theta&=360^\circ-\alpha\approx312^\circ\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}7\cos\theta&=9.729-3\\7\cos\theta&=6.729\\\cos\theta&=\frac{6.729}{7}\end{align*}$$

The related angle is $\alpha=\cos^{-1}(\frac{6.729}{7})\approx15.9950^\circ$. Cosine is positive in quadrants I and IV.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=\alpha\approx16^\circ\\\theta&=360^\circ-\alpha\approx344^\circ\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}9\sin\theta&=-10.733+2\\9\sin\theta&=-8.733\\\sin\theta&=-\frac{8.733}{9}\end{align*}$$

The related angle is $\alpha=\sin^{-1}(\frac{8.733}{9})\approx76.0089^\circ$. Sine is negative in quadrants III and IV.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ+\alpha\approx256^\circ\\\theta&=360^\circ-\alpha\approx284^\circ\end{align*}$$
